solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bravo! Keen-eyed bird sees dog

parts.note: Bravo is B in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the eagle is famed for its sharp eyesight

explanation.surface: A sharp-sighted bird of prey spots a dog below and is cheered on.
explanation.definitionFit: A beagle is a small hound breed, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Corresponding but never meeting

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means similar or analogous
... lines run side by side and never meet

explanation.surface: Two things that match yet never touch, like a pair of long-distance pen pals.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallel cases correspond to each other, and in geometry parallel lines never intersect.

clue.text: Sculpture in future going up

indicators.note: one word is placed inside another, the sculpture sitting in the future

parts.note: coming, as in the coming year, means future
a bust is a sculpted head and shoulders

explanation.surface: An art critic predicts a sculptor's reputation will rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going up' looks like rising in value, but here it means going up in flames.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going up in smoke is burning, which is what combusting describes.

clue.text: Person unknown from a Crown Dependency

parts.note: man can mean any person or human being
in algebra x is the classic unknown quantity

explanation.surface: An anonymous individual hails from one of Britain's offshore territories.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a Crown Dependency, self-governing but under the British Crown; Manx is its adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Manx is the adjective for things belonging to the Isle of Man, a Crown Dependency.

clue.text: Strangely evil crime pinching pound for food

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight between, so one letter is gripped inside the mixed letters
strangely signals that the words evil crime are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A wicked offence involves pocketing a pound to pay for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' scrambles EVIL CRIME and 'pinching' puts L into the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermicelli is a thin pasta, so it is a kind of food.

clue.text: Buzz from live lines

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
LL is the abbreviation for lines, doubled L as with pp for pages

explanation.surface: An excited hum coming from live electrical wires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzz' is informal British for a phone call, as is 'bell': 'give me a bell'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang both a buzz and a bell mean a telephone call.

clue.text: Church leader out in Peru, bishop finds winged child

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which goes out of Peru

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: With a church head gone off to Peru, a bishop discovers an angelic infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church leader' looks like one piece, but CHURCH gives CH and 'leader out' strips the first letter from PERU.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is depicted in art as a chubby infant angel with wings.

clue.text: Function after hearing test

indicators.note: after places the word for function behind the word for hearing

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
to run is to function or operate, as a machine runs

explanation.surface: A machine is checked to see that it works once a hearing is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run is a rehearsal or test performed before the real thing.

clue.text: Girl to chatter idly about love and vanish

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for chatter goes round the letter for love

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly at length
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A young woman gossips about romance and then disappears.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquids evaporate and disappear, so the word is used loosely for things that vanish.

clue.text: Volatile chemical bonds without shell

indicators.note: the shell of a word is its outer letters, here removed from both ends

parts.note: tethers are ropes or bonds that tie something down

explanation.surface: An unstable compound whose chemical bonds lack an outer layer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonds' looks like chemistry; it is TETHERS, and 'without shell' removes its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether is a highly volatile, flammable liquid once used as an anaesthetic.

clue.text: Kiss with reclusive star ingesting ecstasy? It makes a change

indicators.note: ingesting means taking in, so the drug letter goes inside the star's name

parts.note: Greta Garbo, the screen star famous for wanting to be alone
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A recluse film star taking a party drug and blowing kisses would be quite a change.
explanation.definitionFit: A gearbox is the mechanism that changes gear in a vehicle.

clue.text: Musical nun sustaining note brings complaint

indicators.note: sustaining means holding up, so the nun's name holds the note within

parts.note: Maria is the nun in the musical The Sound of Music
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A singing nun holds a long note and someone grumbles about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance but means an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint can mean an ailment, and malaria is a disease spread by mosquitoes.

clue.text: Fish skin showing no sign of phosphorus

indicators.note: showing no sign of means the element's symbol is missing from the word

parts.note: peel is the skin of a fruit
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A fish's skin turns out not to glow with phosphorescence.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a long snakelike fish.

clue.text: Old court to stiffen caution for motorists

parts.note: to starch fabric is to stiffen it
the amber traffic light warns drivers to prepare to stop

explanation.surface: An ancient tribunal toughens its warnings to drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Star Chamber was an English court abolished in 1641, notorious for arbitrary judgments.
explanation.definitionFit: The Star Chamber was a historic English court, hence an old court.

clue.text: Revelation in a curtailed ballad Poe's penned

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, as in a pen, so Poe's name surrounds the shortened song

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer; Poe's means Poe has

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a calypso is a Caribbean song, here standing in for a ballad

explanation.surface: A doom-laden revelation turns up in a shortened ballad Poe has written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' looks like 'written' but signals enclosure, and the calypso standing in for a ballad is a Caribbean song.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelation, the last book of the Bible, is also called the Apocalypse.

clue.text: Staff writer's time in a secure environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds, so the a and secure pieces surround the writer's time

parts.note: to lock something is to secure it
a pen is a writer, so writer's gives pens

explanation.surface: A staff writer works in a safe, protected setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff writer' looks like one phrase, but 'Staff' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpenstock is a long iron-tipped staff used by mountain climbers.

clue.text: Maryland city where there's no more curry?

indicators.note: where there's no signals that a word is removed from the city's name

parts.note: Baltimore is the largest city in Maryland

explanation.surface: A puzzled diner asks in Baltimore why the curry has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: The balti is a curry popularised in Birmingham, cooked and served in a wok-like pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a style of curry cooked in a bowl-shaped pan.

clue.text: Swimmer appearing angry when losing time

indicators.note: when losing signals that a letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: bristling means showing anger, like a dog's raised hair

explanation.surface: A swimmer looks furious when beaten against the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person; it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisling is a small fish, the sprat, often canned; a swimmer is crossword shorthand for a fish.

clue.text: One swoops near ground, moving left to right

indicators.note: the leftmost letter shifts over to the right-hand end of the word

parts.note: low means close to the ground

explanation.surface: A bird of prey glides close to the earth, sweeping across from left to right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a direction but also stands for L, the letter that moves.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl hunts by swooping silently down on its prey.

clue.text: Nature god banking silver for his devotee?

indicators.note: banking means holding safely, as a bank holds money, so the god holds the silver

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of nature and the wild
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A god of the wild stashes away silver, perhaps for a follower.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the god: a worshipper of Pan would be a pagan.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan follows pre-Christian religions, so one might worship Pan.

clue.text: Bush in suitable place one assumed originally

parts.note: a garden is the suitable place for a bush
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A shrub growing somewhere fitting, which someone took for granted at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: One new insult with people causing resentment

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a dig is a cutting remark
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A fresh slight against a whole people stirs up anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Indignation is anger at unfair treatment, close to resentment.

clue.text: Temperature in river good man can't stand

indicators.note: in places the temperature letter inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and also in Wales and England
ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A decent fellow cannot bear the cold of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can't stand' reads as unable to stay upright; it is a verb meaning to hate.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something is to loathe it, so you can't stand it.

clue.text: Men from the east caught enormous bird

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers, hence men
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Soldiers out east trap a giant bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a gigantic mythical bird of Arabian legend, as in Sinbad.

clue.text: Copper bars — they're surely found in Havana

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to bar is to ban, so bars gives bans

explanation.surface: Bars of copper turn up, presumably in the Cuban capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman; it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Havana is the capital of Cuba, so its residents are naturally Cuban.

clue.text: Unidentified illness keeps Italian in service

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the illness holds the Italian letters

parts.note: the lurgy is British slang for an unspecified, catching illness

explanation.surface: A mystery bug keeps an Italian away from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The dreaded lurgy' is a jokey British name for any unidentified illness, from The Goon Show.
explanation.definitionFit: A liturgy is the set form of a religious service.

clue.text: Fish in streams

definitions.meaning: flat fish such as skate and stingrays

explanation.surface: Fish found swimming in streams.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are cartilaginous fish, and beams of light are also called rays.

clue.text: Choking smoke beginning to burn Basil?

parts.note: pother is an old word for a choking cloud of smoke or dust

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A cook's herbs give off acrid smoke as they start to burn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basil' could be a man's name; the question mark shows it is an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A potherb is a leafy plant grown for cooking, and basil is one example.

clue.text: It's a fool that covers king in some butter

indicators.note: covers means encloses, so the butter goes round the letter for king

parts.note: a pat is a small portion of butter
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Only an idiot would smother a monarch in butter.
explanation.definitionFit: Prat is British slang for a stupid or foolish person.

clue.text: Any number stay drunk and abusive

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Plenty of people stay on, get drunk and turn rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty can mean spiteful or insulting, as abusive remarks are.

clue.text: Pole ground contains where Henry's buried

indicators.note: buried means placed deep inside, so the letter goes within the mixed letters
ground, as in ground down, signals the word contains is broken up

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A post set in the earth marks the spot where a man called Henry lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' could be a person from Poland; it is an upright post.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanchion is an upright post or bar used as a support.
